plain.li: [di:entry] Rain all day. Mended the roof, which leaked on me while I mended it, out of spite.
[di:entry] Nothing happened. I wrote that down so there would be a record of it.
[di:entry,!w:tribal] Market. Bought nothing, sold less, talked to everyone. A good day.
[di:entry] The {ANIMALS} were out on the ridge at dawn. I stood and watched them until the porridge burned.
[di:entry] Argued with the neighbour about the fence. Won. Lost the fence.
[di:entry] Couldn't sleep. Sat up with the lamp and thought about the road, and where it goes, and who is at the other end of it.
[di:entry,season:winter] Cold. Very cold. Wrote this with my gloves on, which is why it looks like this.
[di:entry,season:summer] Hot. Too hot to do anything but lie in the shade and plan what I will do when it is cooler.
[di:entry,season:spring] The first green on the trees. Everyone is in a better mood, even the goat.
[di:entry,season:autumn] Picked the last of the {PLANT}. Everything smells of it. I do not mind.
[di:entry] Fixed the gate. Third time this season. The gate and I have an understanding now: it breaks, and I fix it.
[di:entry,!first] Read your last letter again. Laughed at the same part.
[di:entry] Walked out to the edge of the fields and back. Thought about nothing. Highly recommended.
[di:entry] A stranger asked the way. Gave it. Wondered all afternoon where they were going.
[di:entry,grave] A bad day. I will not write about it. I am writing this instead, so the page is not empty.
[di:entry,w:tribal] The second day of the rains. The children made boats of bark and raced them down the gully.
[di:entry,w:tribal] Hunted. Caught nothing. Told a good story about it anyway.
[di:entry,w:spacer] The terminal crashed again. Wrote this by hand, which I had forgotten how to do. It is coming back.
[di:entry,di:latest] Wrote to {TO} at last. You are reading it.
[di:entry,di:latest] Sat down to write to {TO}, and copied out these pages instead, which is cheating, but kindly meant.
[di:entry,di:latest,!first] Your letter came. Read it twice, then once more aloud, to whoever would listen.
[di:break] Someone is at the door. I will finish this later.
[di:break] The pot is boiling over. Back soon.
[di:break] The light is going and the lamp oil is low, so I will stop here and go on in the morning.
[di:break,w:tribal] The fire is low. I will finish this when the sun comes.
[di:break,w:spacer] Power cut. Finishing tomorrow.
[di:resume] Morning now. Where was I? It does not matter. Here is the rest.
[di:resume] It was nothing, as it turned out. The neighbour wanted to borrow a ladder. I lent the ladder and kept the letter.
[di:resume] It is the next day, and I have read over what I wrote, and I am sending it anyway.
[di:resume] Back. The pot is fine. The stove is not. That is another letter.
[di:resume,w:tribal] The sun is up. The fire is new. I go on.
[olde,di:entry] Rain all the day. Mended the roof, which wept upon me while I mended it, out of spite.
[olde,di:entry] Naught befell. I set it down that there be a record of it.
[olde,di:entry] Market day. Bought naught, sold less, spake with all. A good day.
[olde,di:entry] The {ANIMALS} were upon the ridge at dawn. I stood and watched till the pottage burned.
[olde,di:entry,season:winter] Cold, bitter cold. I write this gloved, which is why it is writ so.
[olde,di:entry,!first] Read thy last letter again, and laughed at the same place.
[olde,di:entry,grave] An ill day. I will not write of it.
[olde,di:entry,di:latest] Wrote to {TO} at last. Thou readest it now.
[olde,di:break] Someone knocketh at the door. I will finish this anon.
[olde,di:break] The light faileth and the candle is short, so I stop here and go on at morn.
[olde,di:resume] It is morn now. Where was I? No matter. Here is the rest.
[olde,di:resume] It was naught but a neighbour wanting a ladder. I lent the ladder and kept the letter.
[sv:ancient,di:entry] Rose. Considered the century. Retired.
[sv:ancient,di:entry] A visitor asked my age. I told them. They did not believe me. I did not insist.
[sv:ancient,di:entry] Reordered the archive by colour, then by smell, then back. A productive day.
[sv:ancient,di:entry,di:latest] Began a letter to {TO}. Finished it. Unusually prompt of me.
[di:entry] Mended the fence where the {ANIMALS} come through. Watched the {ANIMALS} come through somewhere else.
[di:entry] Baked. Burned the first batch, ate the second, gave away the third, which was the best, which is always the way.
[di:entry] Long walk to the far field and back. Nothing to report except the sky, which was very large today.
[di:entry,grave] Sat with someone who needed sitting with. Did not say much. Did not need to.
[di:entry,di:latest,fam:familiar|fam:close] Sat down to write to {TO}. The usual chair, the usual lamp, the usual too much to say.
[di:entry,di:latest,fam:new] Began a letter to {TO}, whom I have never met. Crossed out the first line four times.
[di:entry,!first,fam:familiar|fam:close] Took out your old letters and read three of them. Laughed at the same places. Some of them are going soft at the folds.
[di:entry,season:autumn] The first frost. Brought in the last of the {PLANT}. The whole house smells of it.
[di:entry,season:spring] Lambs. Mud. Lambs in the mud. Lambs in the kitchen, briefly.
[di:entry,w:spacer] Shuttle overhead at dawn. Logged it, out of habit. Nobody asked me to log it.
[di:entry,w:spacer] Recalibrated the water reclaimer. It now reclaims slightly better and complains slightly louder.
[di:entry,w:spacer] Watched the comms panel blink for an hour. Nothing came through. It was restful.
[di:entry,w:industrial] The mill whistle went at six, and I was already up, which has never happened before and will not happen again.
[di:entry,w:industrial] Wrote out the accounts. They do not balance. They have never balanced. I suspect they are not meant to.
[di:entry,w:tribal] Walked to the river with the young ones. Showed them where the fish sleep. They did not believe me until the fish woke up.
[di:entry,w:tribal] The hunters came back. Enough meat for the moon. The dogs are smiling.
[di:entry,w:tribal] Sat by the fire and mended a net and listened to the old ones argue about a story that happened before any of them were born.
[di:entry,w:tribal,di:latest] Asked the one who makes marks to put down these words for {TO}. Watched the marks come. They look like birds walking.
[di:break,w:tribal] The fire is low and the story-teller is starting. I will put down the rest at first light.
[di:resume,w:tribal] It is light. The story went on until the stars faded. I will tell it to you another time.
[di:entry,their:scholars] Spent the day in the archive. Found a letter from a hundred years ago complaining about the weather. Nothing changes.
[di:entry,their:salvagers] The Wheel moved on six miles. Found a door in the dirt. Did not open it. We have rules about doors.
[di:entry,their:crew] Hull inspection. Talked to the ship while I worked. The ship did not answer, which is normal, and also lucky.
[di:entry,their:seers] Read the glass at dawn: rain by noon. It rained at dusk. The glass and I are not speaking.
[di:entry,their:traders] Counted the takings twice. Got two different numbers. Took the larger. Business is good.
[di:entry,their:herders] Moved the herd to the high grass. The herd moved itself, really. I followed and took the credit.
[olde,di:entry] Mended the hedge where the {ANIMALS} come through. Watched the {ANIMALS} come through elsewhere.
[olde,di:entry] Baked. Burnt the first batch, ate the second, gave away the third, which was the best, as ever it is.
[olde,di:entry,season:autumn] The first frost. Brought in the last of the {PLANT}, and the whole house smelleth of it.
[olde,di:entry,theirs] To the market cross at {TOWN}. Sold the eggs, bought a ribbon, and know not why I bought it.
[olde,di:entry] The bell rang thrice for vespers, and once more after, for no cause any could tell me.
[olde,di:entry,grave] Sat up with one that needed sitting with. Said little. There was no need.
[olde,di:entry,di:latest,fam:familiar|fam:close] Sat down to write to {TO}, in the wonted chair, by the wonted candle, with too much to say, as ever.
[olde,di:entry,their:healers] Three came with fevers, one with a broken arm, and one for the company. All five were tended.
[olde,di:entry,their:pilgrims] Walked nine miles. Prayed at two shrines. Ate at one inn. Slept in a hayloft, which was holier than it soundeth.
[olde,di:entry,their:sextons] Rang the bell for old Mother Agnes, that was ninety and had planned the whole of it, down to the hymns.
[olde,di:break] The bell ringeth for supper, and I will not miss it, not even for thee. Anon.
[olde,di:resume] Fed, and warm, and back at the letter. Where was I? Here.
[sv:ancient,di:entry] Watched a tree I planted in my second century fall in a storm. Planted another. One must keep one's hand in.
[sv:ancient,di:entry] Received a visitor who wished to know my secret. Told them: patience, and avoid the sun. Neither was what they had hoped.
[sv:ancient,di:entry,!first] Reread the correspondence. Yours is the only one of this century that I reread.
[sv:machine,di:entry] LOG: SUNRISE OBSERVED. DURATION OF OBSERVATION: LONGER THAN NECESSARY. NO CORRECTIVE ACTION TAKEN.
[sv:machine,di:entry] LOG: ASSISTED WITH THE HARVEST. HUMANS SANG. THIS UNIT DID NOT SING. THIS UNIT KEPT TIME.
[sv:machine,di:entry] LOG: A CHILD ASKED IF THIS UNIT DREAMS. THIS UNIT SAID NO. THIS UNIT IS RECONSIDERING.
[sv:machine,di:entry,di:latest] LOG: BEGAN CORRESPONDENCE TO {TO}. DRAFTS: 6. THIS IS DRAFT 7.
[sv:machine,di:break] LOG ENTRY INTERRUPTED: MAINTENANCE CYCLE. RESUMING AFTER.
[sv:machine,di:resume] LOG ENTRY RESUMED. ALL SYSTEMS NOMINAL. CONTINUING.
[sv:beast,di:entry] Rain. Lay in the den. Smelled the rain. Good day.
[sv:beast,di:entry] Found a new trail by the creek. Followed it. It went in a circle. Followed it again, to be sure.
[sv:beast,di:entry] The young ones fought over a stick. Then over a better stick. Then they slept on both.
[sv:beast,di:entry,di:latest] Sat down, two-leg fashion, to make marks for {TO}. Hard on the back. Worth it.
[sv:green,di:entry] Sun all morning. Drank it. Cloud in the afternoon. Waited.
[sv:green,di:entry] Grew a little. Not enough to see. Enough to know.
[sv:green,di:entry] A bird sat on one of us for an hour. Nobody minded. The bird sang. Good.
[sv:green,di:entry,di:latest] Turned toward {TO}, the way we turn toward light. Wrote this.
[di:entry] Wrote a list of things to do. Did the first one. Rewrote the list.
[di:entry] Rain again. The roof held. I sat under it feeling very pleased with the roof.
[di:entry] Helped with a birth at the end of the lane. Mother and child well. I am less well; I have not slept.
[di:entry] Someone knocked at dusk asking the way to somewhere I had never heard of. Gave directions anyway. Hope they find it.
[di:entry,!w:tribal] Went to market with eggs. Came back with a chair. Do not ask how.
[di:entry,season:winter] Too cold to do anything but sit by the fire and think about doing things. Thought about a great many.
[di:entry,di:latest,!first] Read your letter again before beginning this one, {TO}, to remind myself what I owe you a reply to.
[di:break] The kettle is boiling over. I will finish this tomorrow, with tea.
[di:resume] Tomorrow, as promised, with tea. The kettle survived. So did I.
[di:entry,empire] Audience in the morning, banquet in the evening, and between them an hour alone in the garden, which was the best of it.
[di:entry,empire] Bowed to fourteen people today. Was bowed to by two. The arithmetic of rank is unforgiving.
[olde,di:entry] Wrote a list of tasks. Did the first. Wrote the list anew.
[olde,di:entry] Rain again. The roof held. I sat beneath it right pleased with the roof.
[olde,di:entry,season:winter] Too cold for aught but to sit by the fire and think upon doing things. Thought upon a great many.
[olde,di:entry] One knocked at dusk asking the way to a place I had never heard of. Gave directions all the same, and wished them good speed.
[di:entry] Planted beans. A bird watched me do it, and then, I am fairly sure, unplanted them.
[di:entry] Nobody argued at supper. I am not sure what it means. I am keeping an eye on everyone.
[di:entry,season:summer] Too hot to work, so we did not. Sat in the river until our fingers wrinkled and our troubles floated off downstream.
[di:entry,season:autumn] Raked leaves. The wind unraked them. We have agreed to call it a draw.
[di:entry,w:tribal] Saw a hawk take a fish from the river and drop it on the bank. Took the fish. The hawk and I have an understanding now, or the hawk has a grudge.
